title: An Economy of the Future that Works for All
what_it_is: An Economy of the Future that Works for All

sections.label: EDB investment and jobs trend
sections.summary: EDB fixed asset investment rose for three years while expected jobs and value added fell.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Economic Development Board (EDB) committed $14.2 billion of fixed asset investment last year, up from $13.5 billion the year before and $12.7 billion the year before that – so three years rising.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But for it, we get the opposite trend in jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2023, 20,000 jobs; in 2024, 18,700 jobs; and last year 15,700 jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The value added expected went from $26.7 billion to $23.5 billion to $18 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, even on official statistics, the engine of investment to jobs is faltering.

sections.label: Singapore rate lags advanced economies
sections.summary: Singapore's rate, at about 40%, lags most advanced economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Ours, at about 40%, lags most advanced economies.

sections.label: Productivity and income growth gap
sections.summary: Labour productivity grew 2.5% yearly from 2016 to 2024 while real mean income grew 1.3% yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Overall, labour productivity has grown by 2.5% per year from 2016 to 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But over the same period, real mean income only grew at 1.3% per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: From 2016 to 2024, according to the International Labour Organization (ILO), Singapore's output per worker grew 2.3% per year, outstripping major economies, such as the United States (US) at 1.6%, Israel at 1.6%, Hong Kong at 1.3%, Korea at 1.3% and Switzerland at 1.1%.

sections.label: Market land value proposition
sections.summary: The proposition is that Singapore should stop treating market land value as a natural price for socially productive land use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We do not ask a child for an immediate pay-off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, the proposition: Singapore should stop treating market land value as a natural price for every socially productive use of land.

sections.label: Special zone around NTU
sections.summary: A special zone around NTU is proposed where state land is charged as cost recovery and returns come from companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The bargain has four parts: a place to live, near where the work and the research happen; at a price a starting salary can carry, in service of something the country needs – more local enterprise and R&D – with the upside staying with the risk-takers and a say in the rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What we should create a special zone surrounding Nanyang Technological University (NTU), where the state land is charged as cost recovery rather than market scarcity value and takes its returns in the companies that grow there, rather than rent.

sections.label: Development cost of completed flats
sections.summary: In December 2022 the Government put the development cost of 13,506 completed flats at $396,000 each.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In December 2022, the Government put the development cost of that year's 13,506 completed flats at $396,000 each – $234,000 of land against $154,000 of construction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Land was 59% of the cost of a flat.

sections.label: NTU expansion and Bahar land
sections.summary: NTU can still expand unlike NUS, and 116 hectares adjoining NTU are planned for Bahar and CleanTech Park.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And unlike the National University of Singapore (NUS), whose Kent Ridge and One-North districts have little room left, NTU can still expand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And yet, what is planned for Bahar and CleanTech Park, with 116 hectares adjoining NTU?

sections.label: Jurong Innovation District Bahar precinct
sections.summary: The 620-hectare Jurong Innovation District holds Bahar as the next greenfield precinct, already zoned with an Environmental Impact Assessment underway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Jurong Innovation District, 620 hectares, holds in Bahar the next greenfield precinct, already zoned with the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) underway.

sections.label: Johor Zone Agreement signing
sections.summary: The Johor Zone Agreement was signed in January 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, the Johor Zone Agreement was signed in January 2025.

sections.label: NTU and co-living room rents
sections.summary: NTU rooms cost about $412 to $657 monthly, while SG Youth co-living rooms start at $1,800 to $2,000 before utilities and deposits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At NTU this academic year, a non-air-conditioned double room costs about $412 a month, and an air-conditioned single room about $657.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the co-living scheme announced in late July this year, under the SG Youth plan, a room starts at $1,800 a month at 1925 Quarters; $1,950 at Coliwoo Boon Lay and $2,000 at Coliwoo Lutheran, before utilities and deposits – roughly 30% below the usual rate, with operators absorbing the difference.

sections.label: Per-head housing cost calculation
sections.summary: A 500 square foot unit at $200 per square foot, amortised over 10 years at 5%, comes to about $380 a head monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A 500 square foot unit at $200 a square foot – above the construction cost implied by the Government's own 2022 figures, so, it is a conservative assumption and not a hopeful one – if you put three people in it and amortise over 10 years at 5%, it comes out to about $1,061 a month, or $2.12 per square foot, roughly $380 a head, with a sinking fund in.

sections.label: Campus use cap and visa changes
sections.summary: The speaker proposes lifting URA's 5% or 30,000 square metre cap on non-academic campus use and hastening visa decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These are lease terms and not statutes with already existing latitude.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We should lift the Urban Redevelopment Authority's (URA's) planning circular, capping non-academic use of a campus at 5% of floor area or 30,000 square metres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We can hasten visa decisions for deep-tech researchers and for the people the enterprises need, and aim to have every major decision in such a zone made within two weeks.

sections.label: Zhongguancun zone investment arm
sections.summary: The zone's state-owned Oriza Holdings was incorporated in 2001, and China's New Third Board began in 2006 as a Zhongguancun pilot, going nationwide in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The zone grew its own investment arm, Oriza Holdings – state-owned, controlled by the Parks Administration Committee, incorporated in 2001, with about US$14 billion under management today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: China's New Third Board, its national over-the-counter equity market for unlisted small companies, began in 2006 as a Zhongguancun Science Park Share Transfer pilot and went nationwide in 2013.

sections.label: Proposed zone around NTU
sections.summary: The speaker asks for a zone around NTU, a new restricted tenure land use category, and a zone authority taking stakes in enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Speaker, the zone is one bounded, reversible way to try on available land at a price that takes nothing from the reserves, with land prices outside the zone exactly the way they were – a way to make more Singaporeans involved in enterprise and R&D, and not only employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, the ask is threefold: a zone around NTU; a new use category for restricted tenure, non-tradable, mixed housing and enterprise land, valued as the restricted interest it is; and a zone authority that runs its own operations and takes stakes in the enterprises it grows.

sections.label: WP Motion on future economy
sections.summary: The WP moved a Motion to create an economy of the future, aiming to shift from an MNC-centric model to an SME-focused one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singaporeans deserve serious answers; and serious answers are what the WP will provide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: That is why we have moved this Motion to create an economy of the future that works for all.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I cannot agree more that we need both dynamic local companies and opportunities for businesses to succeed, which is why my contribution to this debate will focus on how we can wean ourselves away from a top-down foreign investment, reliant multinational corporation- (MNC-) centric economic model; and instead build a bottom-up domestic capital led small and medium enterprise- (SME-) focused one.

sections.label: Institutions and low tax climate
sections.summary: Emphasis on quality institutions, low taxes, property rights, rule of law and civil service raised per capita income from about $1,600 to over $121,000.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We also placed emphasis on quality institutions and attractive low tax climate, respect for property rights and rule of law and a high functioning civil service.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We fired on all these cylinders, which brought us famously from a per capita income of around $1,600 at Independence; to more than $121,000 today – a massive increase by any stretch of the imagination.

sections.label: Lagging productivity growth
sections.summary: A known design flaw in relentlessly accumulating inputs to production has left productivity growth lagging.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Perhaps the most damning drawback is a known design flaw in the relentless pursuit of accumulating inputs to production, we have lagged in productivity growth.

sections.label: Pivot from MNCs to SMEs
sections.summary: Singapore must evolve away from reliance on foreign MNCs and pivot toward SMEs as its homegrown economic engine.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For starters, we must evolve away from our traditional reliance on foreign MNCs as a driver of our growth and pivot toward SMEs as our homegrown economic engine.

sections.label: SMEs role in economy
sections.summary: Small firms drive destructive innovation and startups sustain growth, but Singapore SMEs contribute only half of value added despite employing seven in ten workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Research shows that worldwide, small firms drive destructive innovation, and startups are the bulwark of sustainable growth through this process of creative destruction.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, while SMEs account for 99 out of 100 registered enterprises here and provide jobs for seven out of 10 Singaporean workers, they currently only contribute to half of the economy's value added.

sections.label: SMEs low productivity
sections.summary: SMEs struggle with low productivity, which the Government has explicitly acknowledged.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Most notably, SMEs struggle with low levels of productivity, something that the Government itself has explicitly acknowledged.

sections.label: SMEs as development innovation
sections.summary: SMEs must be the source of development innovation, the 'D' in R&D, as Singapore's R&D is under 2% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our SMEs must stand ready to be the source of development innovation, the "D" in R&D.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I have shared with this House previously about how at less than 2% of GDP, our nation's R&D remains squarely below the global average and significantly behind that of leading innovation nations.

sections.label: ESR and R&D funding
sections.summary: The ESR talks about R&D but does not underscore the pivot's importance, noting a $37 billion commitment announced last year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The ESR talks about R&D, but it does not underscore the importance of this pivot.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I note that the Prime Minister's Office announced last year a $37 billion commitment to research, innovation and enterprise funding over the next five years.

sections.label: R&D tax incentives
sections.summary: Corporate R&D tax incentives are generous, with up to 400% deduction for the first $400,000 and up to 100% Refundable Investment Credit.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To be fair, tax incentives for corporations to undertake R&D are already very generous, with up to 400% deduction for the first $400,000 of qualifying expenditures every assessment year, supplemented more recently by up to 100% in Refundable Investment Credit.

sections.label: Rent increase cap
sections.summary: One strategy is to cap the maximum annual rent increase at the historical rate of about 3%, limiting the rate not the level.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One simple strategy is to cap the maximum quantum that rents may increase every year to the historical increase of about 3% annually.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is a limit on the rate, not the level.

sections.label: Government landlords and dependency ratio
sections.summary: The speaker says limiting changes to Government and agency landlords would be a major step, and suggests revisiting the dependency ratio ceiling for sectors like F&B.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even if we limit it to Government and agency landlords, such as the HDB or JTC, it will be a major step forward.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It may also be time to revisit the dependency ratio ceiling for certain sectors, like F&B, where Singaporeans continue to shun open positions that are advertised even at attractive wages.

sections.label: ITE and university student supply
sections.summary: In 2024, ITE supplied 1,300 students and autonomous universities sent 800, with around 300 firms joining such programmes, under 1% of registered SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2024, the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) supplied 1,300 students while autonomous universities sent 800.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Around 300 firms have joined such programmes, which are less than 1% of registered SMEs.

sections.label: Grants paired with skills transfer
sections.summary: Larger grants should be paired with a clear proposal and timetable for skills transfer, including possibly sunsetting foreign Employment Passes if no additional transfer occurs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Larger grants in particular should be paired with a clear proposal and timetable for ensuring skills transfer, including the possibility of a sunset of foreign Employment Passes after a designated duration if no additional transfer is taking place.

sections.label: Not a wholesale model overhaul
sections.summary: The speaker clarifies he is not calling for a wholesale overhaul of the GLC-heavy, MNC-led and foreign capital-reliant model, which has served Singapore well.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: To be clear, what I am calling for is not a wholesale overhaul of our GLC-heavy, MNC-led and foreign capital-reliant model, which has to date served us well.

sections.label: Shifts to favour homegrown firms
sections.summary: The speaker calls for policy and institutional shifts to place small and especially medium-sized firms at the heart of the economic model, away from large foreign MNCs and GLCs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: No modern economy, much less a globalised one, like ours, operates without due attention to international players.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: But what I am calling for are policy and institutional shifts that will usher in a changed mindset for how we should view our homegrown companies in an already wealthy, advanced economy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The shift will place small, but especially, medium-sized firms at the beating heart of our nation's economic model, away from the interests of large foreign-based MNCs or even our GLC behemoths.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: By destroying, we will create simultaneously an economy ready for the 21st century.

sections.label: Q2 growth and business costs
sections.summary: Singapore's economy grew 5.7% in the second quarter, with manufacturing up 12.2% on AI-related demand, while many businesses face uncertain demand and high costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, Singapore's economy grew by 5.7% in the second quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Manufacturing expanded by 12.2%, driven largely by AI-related demand for electronics and precision engineering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many businesses, especially domestic-facing ones, continue to grapple with uncertain demand and persistently high manpower, rental and operating costs.

sections.label: Engagement sessions and adopted recommendations
sections.summary: 25 engagement sessions brought stakeholders together, and 24 of 27 recommendations were adopted, including manpower, lease, solar and SME office changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It brought businesses, trade associations and chambers and public agencies together through 25 engagement sessions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So far, 24 of 27 recommendations has been adopted in some shape and form.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These included changes to foreign manpower sources for select occupations; retention of experienced Work Permit holders; more flexible industrial leases; faster solar-panel deployment approvals; and the creation of the SME Pro-Enterprise Office.

sections.label: SBF overseas projects facilitation
sections.summary: SBF facilitated 108 overseas projects for 79 Singapore companies across 44 markets, including an agri-food firm's RM50 million Johor investment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To grow, Singapore companies must venture abroad, find new customers, build new production capacity, acquire technology and participate in supply chains beyond our shores.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So far, SBF has facilitated 108 overseas projects for 79 Singapore companies across 44 markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With SBF's facilitation, this Singapore agri-food company invested more than RM50 million to establish a new manufacturing capacity in Johor, Malaysia, while retaining Singapore as the base for managing its regional business.

sections.label: RTS Link cross-border spending
sections.summary: After the RTS Link opens, Singapore consumers could spend an additional $1.05 billion annually in Johor Bahru and Johor visitors $756 million in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: After the RTS Link opens, Singapore consumers could spend an additional $1.05 billion annually in Johor Bahru, while Johor visitors could spend an additional $756 million in Singapore.

sections.label: Companies and EmployWell participation
sections.summary: Over 5,200 companies took part in these programmes, and EmployWell gave over 2,100 individuals employability support, with more than 1,000 re-entering the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More than 5,200 companies have taken part in these programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Through EmployWell alone, over 2,100 individuals facing barriers to work received employability support, and more than 1,000 re-entered the workforce.

sections.label: Business diversification and support measures
sections.summary: Businesses are diversifying investments and the Government introduced support measures, while AI raises energy demand and an ageing population raises workforce and consumer concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Businesses have been actively diversifying their investment and managing risks and the Government has recently introduced a range of support measures that can in the short term ease the pressure faced by SMEs and the people from external pressures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While AI is driving technological transformation, it is also pushing up energy demand and we need to develop renewable energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The ageing population is also a serious concern – an inefficient youth population will lead to a dual shortage of both the workforce and consumer base.

sections.label: Cannot support Motion
sections.summary: The speaker states they cannot support the Motion in its current form.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As such, I cannot support the Motion in its current form.

sections.label: Three economic imperatives
sections.summary: The passage states three imperatives: sharpen Singapore's value proposition, enhance agility and adaptability, and build resilience alongside efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: Its three imperatives are clear: sharpen Singapore's value proposition; enhance agility and adaptability; and build resilience alongside efficiency.

sections.label: Business R&D expenditure 2023
sections.summary: Business expenditure on research and development reached about $9 billion in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: Business expenditure in R&D has reached about $9 billion in 2023.

sections.label: Focus on mutual business support
sections.summary: The passage states focus should be on helping MNCs, large local companies, SMEs and startups build up one another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: Instead, our focus should be on helping MNCs, large local companies, SMEs and startups build up one another.

sections.label: Global partnership builds capabilities
sections.summary: The passage states partnership with a global enterprise can help a Singapore company build proprietary capabilities, move up the value chain and compete globally, noting AEM's market capitalisation is around $2.8 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: This shows how partnership with a global enterprise can help a Singapore company build proprietary capabilities, move up the value chain and compete and win on the world stage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: And I just last checked, AEM's market capitalisation is around $2.8 billion.

sections.label: Exports share of GDP 2025
sections.summary: In 2025, Singapore's exports of goods and services amounted to approximately 178% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: In 2025, Singapore's exports for goods and services amounted to approximately 178% of our GDP.

sections.label: Government help for internationalisation
sections.summary: The passage states the Government can help local enterprises internationalise through market access platforms, financing support, overseas networks, talent development and partnerships with regional governments and businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: The Government can do this to help local enterprises internationalise through market access platforms, financing support, overseas networks, talent development and stronger partnerships with regional governments and businesses.

sections.label: Forward Singapore and ESR focus
sections.summary: The Forward Singapore agenda strengthens social support, and the ESR focuses on good jobs, lifelong learning, enterprise transformation and resilience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: The Forward Singapore agenda strengthens social support across different life stages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: The ESR builds on this by focusing on good jobs, lifelong learning, enterprise transformation and resilience.

sections.label: Companies conferred in three years
sections.summary: In three years the movement has conferred 1,046 companies, over 70% of them local companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: In just three years, the movement has conferred 1,046 companies, more than 70% of them local companies.

sections.label: Open, competitive, inclusive future economy
sections.summary: The future economy must be open, competitive and inclusive, embracing AI to expand human capability and giving every Singaporean a fair chance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: Our future economy must be open, competitive and inclusive at the same time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: We must attract the best from the world while developing the best in Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: We must support local enterprises while staying plugged into a global network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: We must embrace AI and technology, not to replace human capability, but to expand it – using AI to strengthen workers' judgement, free up time for meaningful interactions and support roles where trust remains central.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: It recognises the real anxieties that workers and businesses face, but it also recognises that Singapore cannot respond to uncertainty by becoming smaller in our ambition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: We must strengthen our role as a global trusted hub and we must ensure that every Singaporean has a fair chance to contribute and benefit from the future economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: An economy of the future that works for all is not built by choosing between openness and inclusion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: It is built by making growth translate into good jobs.

sections.label: Four amendments to the Motion
sections.summary: Mr Edward Chia proposed four amendments to the Motion, changing words in lines 1 and 5.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Tiong, hang on, let me go through the process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: There are four amendments proposed by Mr Edward Chia to the Motion: Amendment No 1: "In line 1, to delete 'notwithstanding' and insert 'in line with'.".

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Amendment No 2: "In line 5, to delete 'economic engine driven' and insert 'economy powered'.".

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Amendment No 3: "In line 5, after the words 'local companies,' to insert 'global enterprises,'.".

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Amendment No 4: "In line 5, after the words 'healthy domestic' to insert 'and external'.".

sections.label: Economy powered by both
sections.summary: The speaker says the amendment basically means an economy must be powered by both local companies and global enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: It appears to me, to use a favourite word from a Minister opposite.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: But I think it is basically really saying that an economy must be powered by both local companies and global enterprises.

sections.label: State land ownership and ESR report
sections.summary: The state owns about 90% of Singapore's land, yet land is not mentioned in the ESR report's 32 recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The state owns some 90% of the land in Singapore and it is by a wide margin the biggest landlord in the country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In fact, even as economists often identify the key factors of production, being land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship, there is not a single mention of land in the 32 recommendations of the ESR report, even as the report itself had acknowledged that land, energy and demographic constraints are expected to tighten.

sections.label: Singapore land cost share
sections.summary: A real estate C-suite member said land costs now form roughly 70% of total project development expenditure in Singapore, up from 4% in the 1980s for Raffles City.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As a local C-suite member of one of Asia's largest real estate groups has shared in the past, in Singapore, land costs now form roughly 70% of total project development expenditure, up from just 4% in the 1980s for Raffles City.

sections.label: Reserve price and tender outcomes
sections.summary: The Minister for Law disclosed the reserve price is pegged to 85% of the Chief Valuer's estimated market value, and 17 of 133 sites tendered from 2016 to 2021 were not awarded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In a reply to my Parliamentary Question in July 2021, the Minister for Law disclosed that the reserve price is pegged to 85% of the estimated market value assessed by the Chief Valuer's office; and that of the 133 sites launched for tender between 2016 and 2021, 17 were not awarded because the highest bids were deemed not reflective of the fair market value of the land.

sections.label: Site awarded above refused bid
sections.summary: The site was awarded in April 2015 at $1.67 billion, or $943 per square foot per plot ratio, about two thirds higher than the bid the Government had earlier refused.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: When the site was eventually tended and awarded in April 2015, it was sold at $1.67 billion, or $943 per square foot per plot ratio, at a rate some two thirds higher than the bid the Government had earlier refused.

sections.label: Home loans and mortgage growth
sections.summary: Home loans make up at least 70% of total household liabilities in Singapore, and mortgage borrowing grew 5.8% year on year in the first quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Home loans make up at least 70% of total household liabilities in Singapore and mortgage borrowing grew 5.8% year on year in the first quarter of this year.

sections.label: Compute initiative and firm pairing
sections.summary: An Enterprise Compute Initiative was announced at Budget 2025 with up to $150 million, and by October 2025 some 1,000 firms were reportedly paired with cloud partners, against about 385,000 firms in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the AI economy, compute is to value creation what land was to the industrial economy, the scarce foundational input on which everything else is built.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We have made a start and I acknowledge that an Enterprise Compute Initiative was announced at Budget 2025 with up to $150 million of funding support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: By October 2025, we had reportedly paired some 1,000 firms with cloud partners, but this is a very modest figure as compared to the 385,000 or so firms in Singapore's enterprise landscape in 2024, as identified in the ESR's final report.

sections.label: UK compute and Singapore AI adoption
sections.summary: The UK committed up to £2 billion by 2030 under its Compute Roadmap, while Singapore extracts some $20 billion in land sales proceeds a year but sets aside $150 million for compute and $1 billion over five years for AI research, with 4% of firms embedding AI by 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The United Kingdom (UK) having found itself with only 1.3% of global compute capacity in late 2022, committed up to £2 billion by 2030 under its Compute Roadmap, and its AI Research Resource now allocates compute directly: 10,000 GPU hours for first-time users and 20,000 GPU hours for SMEs, awarded as capacity rather than cash.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We extract some $20 billion in a single year in land sales proceeds also and yet, we are only setting aside $150 million for the digital land on which our own companies must build, and $1 billion over five years in overall national AI research.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And for all our first-place finishes in AI-readiness, only 4% of firms had embedded AI into core business processes by 2026, with adoption at 15% among SMEs, against 63% for larger firms.

sections.label: Expanding compute access
sections.summary: Policy-makers can act by expanding compute access for startups and researchers and investing in shared training assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Policy-makers have an important opportunity to act, such as through expanding access to compute for startups and researchers, and investing in shared training assets.

sections.label: National compute programme subsidies
sections.summary: A national compute programme should offer subsidised allocated capacity to local companies, especially SMEs and entrepreneurs, priced below market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Similarly, a national compute programme should offer a subsidised allocated capacity to local companies and particularly, SMEs and entrepreneurs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This will draw on capacity in which the state has an ownership interest, priced below market with a published rate card with tenure certainty and eligibility weighted towards local ownership and local value capture.

sections.label: Foreign investment tax incentives
sections.summary: Singapore extends generous low tax incentives and charges as low as 5% corporate income tax to attract MNCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Third, we do not apply this stinginess to foreign investment promotion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We extend generous low tax incentives and charge as low as 5% corporate income tax, instead of 17% to attract MNCs via a series of incentive schemes.

sections.label: Economic Strategy Review support
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Economic Strategy Review Committee report and supports the Motion, while noting state rent maximisation and business sentiments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I welcome the final recommendation report of the Economic Strategy Review Committee and I support that Motion moved by Mr Kenneth Tiong and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But, as long as the state remains the most successful rent maximiser in our economy, the grand vision of this strategy will remain only on paper.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The hon Members Assoc Prof Lim and Mr Kenneth Tiong have tapped into a sentiment that some Singaporeans genuinely feel: some business owners feel the economy has grown harder to navigate; some SMEs feel squeezed by costs, including rents, by manpower, and they feel crowded out for business and funding opportunities by larger competition; some workers, including younger workers, wonder if opportunity for them is expanding as fast as the economy itself.

sections.label: MNC-local partnership projects
sections.summary: In 2025, EDB generated 19 MNC-local enterprise partnership projects working with Enterprise Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 2025, working alongside Enterprise Singapore, EDB generated 19 MNC-local enterprise partnership projects.

sections.label: Capability gaps of enterprises
sections.summary: Capability gaps in growth capital, management, technology, networks and risk appetite are closed by making global connections work better for Singaporean enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The constraints are usually different – access to growth capital, management with experience running operations across borders, or leading technology transformation, networks that open overseas markets, risk appetite.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These are capability gaps and they are unlikely to be closed simply by wining ourselves off connections with our global capital.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If anything, they are closed by making those connections work better for many more Singaporean enterprises.

sections.label: Helping Singaporean enterprises compete internationally
sections.summary: The question is whether enough Singaporean enterprises are being helped to connect to ecosystems, gain capabilities, compete internationally and become ecosystem builders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The real question is whether we are helping enough Singaporean enterprises get connected to the ecosystems, acquire the capabilities that allow them to climb the value chain, compete internationally and ultimately, become ecosystem builders themselves.

sections.label: PSA global ports and digital solutions
sections.summary: PSA operates over 70 terminals in 45 countries, and its global port management plus digital technologies, data, automation and AI let it design solutions single-port operators cannot.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Today, it operates over 70 terminals across more than 180 locations in 45 countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Managing ports across the world's major trade routes gives PSA a unique view of global supply chains.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: By combining operational expertise with digital technologies, data, automation and AI to design solutions its customers cannot get from a single-port operator.

sections.label: Ownership, capability and competitiveness
sections.summary: The speaker says targeting ownership before capability and competitiveness means not owning more of the pie, and supports Mr Edward Chia's amendments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Target ownership before capability and competitiveness, and we do not own more of the pie.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: That is why I support the hon Member Mr Edward Chia's amendments.

sections.label: Building an economy of the future
sections.summary: Singapore succeeded by becoming useful and indispensable to the world, and must now build a future economy where more Singaporeans can create, capture and own value.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore never succeeded by asking the world to make room for us.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We succeeded by becoming useful, indispensable to it, even as the world changes around us.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our task is now to continue to build an economy of the future where each reinforces the other, where the best companies, foreign or local, want to be.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And to make sure more Singaporeans have the capability, the confidence and the opportunity to shape that future, to create value, to capture it and increasingly, to own it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So that every generation of Singaporeans begins with opportunities greater than the generation before.

sections.label: Autonomous university graduate employment rates
sections.summary: Among autonomous university graduates, 88.9% of the 2025 cohort secured employment within six months, down from 91.2%, while full-time permanent employment fell to 74.4% from 79.4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Among autonomous- university graduates in the labour force, those who secured employment of any kind within six months of completing their final examinations amounted to 88.9% of the 2025 cohort, a slight drop from 91.2% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It includes graduates in full-time permanent employment; but also, those in part-time, temporary or freelance work; those who have accepted a job that starts later; and those taking steps to start a business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, those in full-time permanent employment amounted to 74.4% of the cohort last year, down from 79.4% the previous year.

sections.label: Private education institution graduate employment
sections.summary: Among surveyed fresh graduates from full-time external degree programmes at private education institutions, 78.9% secured employment and 46.9% were in full-time permanent employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Among surveyed fresh graduates from full-time external degree programmes at private education institutions, 78.9% secured employment and 46.9% were in full-time permanent employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, another 24% were in part-time or temporary work, including 9.7% who said this was involuntary.

sections.label: Fair Start Promise for youths
sections.summary: Proposes a Fair Start Promise, a national commitment to work towards a simple goal for youths, since exposure is not employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Exposure is useful, but exposure is not employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And Mr Speaker, that is why I propose a "Fair Start Promise" to all our youths – a national commitment to work towards a simple goal.

sections.label: Opening entry-level jobs to beginners
sections.summary: Says more ordinary entry-level jobs should be opened to capable beginners, and where real work can develop a beginner, that proper job should be the priority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: First, we should open more ordinary entry-level jobs to capable beginners, where an employer has real work that can develop a beginner through the ordinary course of employment, the priority should be that proper job.

sections.label: SWDA standards for verified competencies
sections.summary: Says the SWDA should establish standards for IHLs and employers to verify projects, internships, Work-Study stints and assessed competencies through the Careers and Skills Passport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The SWDA should establish standards through which the institutes of higher learning (IHLs) and employers can verify substantial projects, internships, Work-Study learning stints and other assessed competencies through the Careers and Skills Passport.

sections.label: Apprenticeship framework and SWDA role
sections.summary: Says GRIT offers short traineeships, but longer occupations need a proper apprenticeship framework with paid employment, employee status, CPF, structured training and portable competences, which SWDA should expand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: GRIT, for example, offers a three- to six-month allowance-based traineeship and can provide useful short-term experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But where an occupation requires sustained, supervised practice over a longer period of time, we need a different, more well-developed route: a proper apprenticeship framework providing paid employment, full employee status, CPF, structured training and portable competences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: SWDA should identify occupations where employers need workers but beginners need sustained workplace training, and work with employers and sector bodies to expand apprenticeship places that meet a common quality floor.

sections.label: Support tied to genuine jobs
sections.summary: Says support should go where employers create genuine additional jobs or apprenticeships that would not proceed on the same terms without help, and procuring agencies can require proportionate commitment without a blanket quota.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Support should be available where an employer can show that they will create a genuine additional employee job or proper apprenticeship, and that the opening would not proceed on the same terms without help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Where workforce development is relevant to a substantial public contract, procuring agencies can require or recognise proportionate commitment to proper apprenticeships and genuine employee entry level roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The purpose is to connect public purchasing demand to the development of Singapore's future workforce without imposing a blanket quota on every contractor.

sections.label: Recovering money for misrepresented roles
sections.summary: Says money should be recovered where an employer misrepresents the role or fails to provide the promised job, wages or development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Money should be recovered where an employer misrepresents the role or fails to provide the job, wages or development promised.

sections.label: SWDA baseline and targets
sections.summary: The SWDA should publish a baseline and staged targets, with results showing how many young people remain without stable employment at six months, for how long and why.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The SWDA should publish a baseline and staged targets for those outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The results must also show how many young people remain without stable employment at the critical six-month mark, for how long and for what broad reasons.

sections.label: Expanding free trade agreements
sections.summary: Singapore must expand its network of free trade agreements with as many countries as possible, including emerging markets, opening new doors for SMEs and services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To do this, we must expand our network of free trade agreements (FTAs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must pursue FTAs with as many countries as possible, not just big economies but also, emerging markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Every new FTA is a new door for our SMEs, a new channel for our services and a new vote of confidence in Singapore's open economy.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore international presence
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore's international presence must be leveraged more aggressively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore's international presence must be leveraged more aggressively.

sections.label: Grants for internationalisation
sections.summary: The Government should enhance grants and financial support to derisk internationalisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government should enhance grants – as what we have seen before – and financial support to derisk internationalisation.

sections.label: SMEs share of enterprises
sections.summary: SMEs make up 99% of Singapore's enterprises and employ about two-thirds of its workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SMEs make up 99% of our enterprises and employ about two-thirds of our workforce.

sections.label: Companies embedding sustainability
sections.summary: As Singapore aims for net-zero by 2050 or earlier, companies must embed sustainability into their operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As Singapore aims for net-zero by 2050 or earlier, companies must embed sustainability into their operations.

sections.label: AI already here
sections.summary: AI is not coming; AI is already here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: AI is not coming; AI is already here.

sections.label: SkillsFuture framework expansion
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture framework is a good start but must go further, allowing training credits for AI tools, memberships and stipends for reskilling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture framework is a good start, but it must go further – allow training credits to be used for subscribing to AI-powered productivity tools, fund memberships in trade associations and chambers, and business networks that provide continuous learning, provide stipends for mid-career workers undergoing reskilling, not as a support but as a programme.

sections.label: Support for displaced workers
sections.summary: For jobs displaced by AI, stronger monthly income support, career conversion programmes, counselling and mental health support are needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For those whose jobs that are displaced by AI, we need stronger monthly income support during retraining, career conversion programmes tailored to growth sectors, counselling and mental health support to manage anxiety and uncertainty.

sections.label: R&D grants and business costs
sections.summary: Government must increase R&D grants and tax incentives, expand the R&D Tax Incentive scheme, create co-funding pools, support pilot projects, review regulatory fees, streamline compliance, provide SME relief and keep housing and transport affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government must increase R&D grants and tax incentives, expand the Research and Development Tax Incentive scheme, create co-funding pools for industry-academia collaborations, support proof-of-concept and pilot projects that bridge the gap between lab and market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Businesses are grappling with rising rents, utilities and manpower costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must review regulatory fees and streamline compliance burdens, provide targeted relief for SMEs in high-cost sectors, ensure housing and transport remain affordable to retain talent.

sections.label: Bridge for trade and excellence
sections.summary: Singapore must be a bridge for trade, become Centres of Excellence, embrace sustainability, prepare the workforce for AI, and build an economy where Singaporeans and enterprises prosper.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must be the bridge for trade, not a barrier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must become the Centres of Excellence – in finance, logistics, transport, education, management, medical, sustainability and AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must embrace sustainability as a competitive advantage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must prepare our workforce for the AI revolution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us build an economy where every Singaporean can prosper, where every enterprise can grow and where our nation continues to punch above its weight on the global stage. : Allow me to do a pantun on this. :   The changing world brings uncertainties; Singapore companies brace and prepare; Steered by the Government's strategies; Together as one, we forge ahead from there. : Mr Speaker, in conclusion, the Motion before us calls for an economy that is equal, inclusive and driven by dynamic local companies.

sections.label: Shrinking local craft workforce
sections.summary: Over the past decade the local craft workforce shrank by 40% to 50%, with only 28% of 186,000 craftsmen and trades workers being locals and a median age of 56.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Over the past decade, the local craft workforce has shrunk by 40% to 50%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Of the 186,000 craftsmen and trades workers in Singapore – only 28% are locals and their ranks are ageing with a median age of 56 years old.

sections.label: Penalties versus unregulated alternatives
sections.summary: Non-compliance carries fines up to $10,000, jail up to three years, or both, yet a gap exists between licensed and unregulated rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While non-compliance carries statutory fines of up to $10,000, a jail term of up to three years, or both, daily practice reveals a massive gap between the rates charged by licensed trades persons and unregulated marketplace alternatives.

sections.label: Electrocution deaths from unsafe wiring
sections.summary: In 2016 a 15-year-old boy and in 2020 an elderly couple and their son were electrocuted after unsafe water heater installation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2016, the improper wiring of a water heater to a three-pin plug by workers unlicensed to do electrical work resulted in the tragic electrocution of a 15-year-old boy in his HDB flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Similarly, in 2020, an elderly couple and their son were electrocuted to death in their Jurong flat due to similar unsafe installation of a water heater.

sections.label: Licensing bottleneck and modular endorsement pathway
sections.summary: Two years of full spectrum practical experience creates a bottleneck, which a modular trade endorsement pathway certifying competencies task by task can resolve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The structural bottleneck lies in the post-graduation licensing requirements of completing two years of relevant practical experience, covering a full spectrum of trade work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Trade practitioners I spoke to have highlighted that in reality, almost no small contractor covers the entire spectrum of work, expecting a residential service plumber to log experience across industrial supply systems creates a practical bottleneck as current evaluation criteria favour multi-year commercial construction projects over day-to-day residential maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We can resolve the licensing bottleneck by implementing a modular trade endorsement pathway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Instead of requiring two years of full spectrum experience before a worker can practise independently, this pathway certifies specific verified competencies task by task.

sections.label: Tradesperson skills ledger platform
sections.summary: A digital tradesperson skills ledger platform would log task-specific endorsements verified under licensed artisans, creating an immutable record of practical milestones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To operationalise these modular endorsements, we need a modern digital architecture, an official tradesperson skills ledger platform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It allows tradespersons to log task-specific trade endorsements, verified under the supervision of licensed artisans, creating an immutable record of their practical milestones.

sections.label: Employer-tied licensing veto power
sections.summary: Rigid employer-tied licensing requirements inadvertently grant employers veto power over an entry-level worker's advancement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Across skilled trades, the Government currently enforces safety through rigid employer-tied licensing requirements, inadvertently, granting employers veto power over an entry-level worker's advancement.

sections.label: ESR engagement numbers
sections.summary: The ESR was informed by more than 80 engagements involving more than 7,700 businesses, workers, unions and trade associations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The ESR was informed by more than 80 engagements involving more than 7,700 businesses, workers, unions and trade associations, some of whom are in this room.

sections.label: Singapore merchandise trade size
sections.summary: In 2025, Singapore's merchandise trade reached almost $1.4 trillion, several times the size of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In 2025, Singapore's merchandise trade reached almost $1.4 trillion, equivalent to several times the size of our GDP.

sections.label: EDB investment commitments 2025
sections.summary: In 2025, EDB secured $14.2 billion in fixed asset investment commitments, expected to create around 15,700 jobs over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In 2025, EDB secured $14.2 billion in fixed asset investment commitments, with the investment commitments expected to create around 15,700 jobs when realised over the next five years.

sections.label: Private R&D and spillovers
sections.summary: Private sector R&D expenditure more than doubled from $4.3 billion in 2013 to $9 billion in 2023, and a 2025 MTI study estimated spillover benefits from EDB-supported firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Private sector R&D expenditure more than doubled from $4.3 billion in 2013 to $9 billion in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A 2025 Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) study estimated that between 2012 and 2019, each EDB-supported firm generated net spillover benefits averaging $48.5 million in value added annually for non-EDB-supported firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Significantly, this spillover benefits accounted for 41% of the firms' total direct and spillover economic contribution and much of this came through the labour market, as skills and capabilities developed in these firms benefited the wider economy.

sections.label: Capability transfer for workers
sections.summary: The Capability Transfer Programme supports foreign specialists transferring capabilities to local workforce and overseas training, and more structured capability transfer could be facilitated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We must help workers move up the same value chain that we want Singapore's economy to move up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We already have the Capability Transfer Programme, supporting companies in bringing foreign specialists to transfer capabilities to our local workforce as well as overseas training for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Could we go further, for example, by facilitating more structured capability transfer from foreign professionals already working here to Singapore colleagues?

sections.label: Foreign manpower policy question
sections.summary: If labour costs are the principal concern, are Members suggesting significantly relaxing foreign manpower policies?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: If labour costs are the principal concern, are Members suggesting that we significantly relax our foreign manpower policies?

sections.label: Trade-offs in policy objectives
sections.summary: Parliament has debated proposals on wages, retirement adequacy and environmental measures, illustrating trade-offs as such measures can affect business cost structures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: At the same time, Parliament has debated proposals before aimed at strengthening wages and retirement adequacy, as well as more ambitious environmental measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: These may be legitimate policy objectives, but they illustrate the trade-offs involved – measures that advance important social or environmental objectives can affect business cost structures So, when we call for lower costs and greater support for local enterprises, I think the next questions should be: what are the concrete policy choices?

sections.label: Committee for Economic Resilience
sections.summary: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs announced the Committee for Economic Resilience, which the speaker co-chairs with Dr Wan Rizal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Within the Malay/Muslim community, the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs has announced the establishment of the Committee for Economic Resilience, which I co-chair with Dr Wan Rizal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We want to listen to the aspirations and economic concerns of our youths, workers, professionals and entrepreneurs, and help translate the ESR recommendations into more tangible opportunities.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim business owners and AI
sections.summary: The passage asks how more Malay/Muslim business owners can use AI to raise productivity, strengthen competitiveness and grow their businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How can we help more Malay/Muslim business owners use AI to raise productivity, strengthen competitiveness and grow their businesses?

sections.label: Youths in emerging sectors
sections.summary: The passage asks whether more young people can enter sectors such as advanced manufacturing, digital technology, AI and the green economy, questions to be examined by the Committee for Economic Resilience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can more of our young people enter sectors such as advanced manufacturing, digital technology, AI, the green economy and other emerging sectors?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: These are among the questions that we want to examine through the Committee for Economic Resilience.

sections.label: Support for Motion with amendments
sections.summary: The speaker says he cannot support the Motion as it stands but will support it with MP Edward Chia's proposed amendments, including replacing the word "engine".

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our challenge is to remain global while ensuring that more Singaporeans, businesses and communities participate in the opportunities our global connections create.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, Mr Speaker, while I support the aspirations underlying this Motion, I cannot support the Motion as it stands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I will, however, support the Motion with the proposed amendments by Member of Parliament Mr Edward Chia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And I will also support, especially the second line, where the word "engine" needs to be replaced, because it is not just a single economic engine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is about the whole economy, powered by multiple factors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It makes the second sentence clearer to me.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The amendment may seem minor but it makes it clearer in that sense.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, that is, in that sense, with the amendments, how we build stronger companies, create better jobs and build an economy of the future that truly works for all.

sections.label: Mandatory retrenchment benefits proposal
sections.summary: The passage proposes mandatory retrenchment benefits funded by joint employer and employee contributions of 0.1% of monthly salary, paying retrenched workers 40% of last drawn salary for up to six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is a policy choice that unfairly disadvantages our workers and leaves them vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We must protect hardworking Singaporeans and legislate mandatory retrenchment benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In contrast to the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme, our proposal is meant to be universal and funded by joint contributions from both employers and employees, amounting to a combined 0.1% of the worker's monthly salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The basic idea is for each retrenched worker to receive 40% of their last drawn salary, which will be further capped at 40% of Singapore's prevailing median income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These payouts will last up to six months at most.

sections.label: Coverage limited to involuntary redundancy
sections.summary: The passage states that coverage is restricted only to cases of involuntary redundancy, eliminating concerns that workers may quit to collect benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, coverage is restricted only to cases of involuntary redundancy, thus eliminating the concerns that workers may quit in order to collect benefits.

sections.label: Education loans and CPF expansion
sections.summary: The Government should offer interest-free education loans to mid-career Singaporeans doing postgraduate degrees and expand the CPF Education Loan Scheme to Master's programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, the Government should directly offer mid-career Singaporeans undertaking a postgraduate degree with access to education loans that are interest free for at least the duration of the course and with repayments to start at a modest rate before progressively increasing after a certain period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, the Government should expand the CPF Education Loan Scheme to cover part-time and full-time Master's programmes at our IHLs.

sections.label: Merger of SkillsFuture and Workforce Singapore
sections.summary: The merger of SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore into one Statutory Board could support workers through displacement, retraining, job matching and re-employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If retraining ends with the worker returning home to search job portals alone, then we have merely replaced one form of insecurity with another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am thus encouraged by the opportunity presented last month by the merger of SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore into a single Statutory Board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: SWDA has the potential to serve a new integrated system where workers can be supported actively by the state throughout the entire process of displacement, retraining, job matching and re-employment.

sections.label: One-stop employment centre caseworkers
sections.summary: SWDA should be a premier one-stop employment centre where every involuntarily unemployed jobseeker gets a dedicated caseworker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: SWDA should serve as a premier one-stop employment centre where every involuntary unemployed jobseeker can be assigned with a dedicated caseworker.

sections.label: Missing outcome data on workforce development
sections.summary: Billions are spent on workforce development but little outcome data is public, including which courses or providers perform better, whether wages rise, or whether workers stay employed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We spend billions of dollars supporting workforce development, but surprisingly, little outcome data enters the public domain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We know, for example, that around 55% of previously unemployed trainees who participated in the SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme found new jobs within six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But we do not know which courses perform better at helping trainees to find new jobs, which providers consistently deliver stronger outcomes, whether wages rise after retraining and whether workers remain employed one year later.

sections.label: Publishing SkillsFuture effectiveness metrics
sections.summary: The Government should publish more metrics so workers can assess how effective specific SkillsFuture programmes are for employment prospects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government should thus publish more metrics to help workers assess the effectiveness of specific SkillsFuture programmes in relation to employment prospects.

sections.label: AGO finding on potential grant gaming
sections.summary: The AGO found six groups of 30-related entities showed patterns suggesting potential gaming of programmes to maximise grant claims rather than genuine training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In page 65 of the report, the AGO found that six group of 30-related entities had engaged in patterns that suggested "potential gaming of the programmes to maximise grant claims rather than genuine training initiatives".

sections.label: Six proposals in speech
sections.summary: The speech recaps six proposals on retrenchment benefits, redundancy insurance, education loans, SWDA consolidation, industry collaboration and outcome data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To recap the proposals in my speech: one, legislating mandatory retrenchment benefits; two, implementing universal redundancy insurance; three, introducing interest-free education loans and allowing CPF to be used for postgraduate studies; four, consolidating SWDA into a one-stop shop for employment and upskilling, with dedicated caseworkers; five, collaborating more closely with industry partners to finetune SkillsFuture offerings and curricula; and six, publishing more public outcome data by provider and course.

sections.label: ESR proactive career bridges
sections.summary: The ESR's proposal for proactive career bridges for workers in at-risk roles is an important step in that direction.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The ESR's proposal for proactive career bridges for workers in at-risk roles is an important step in that direction.

sections.label: Subsidised semesters count against grant
sections.summary: When they transfer programmes, the subsidised semesters already used count against the tuition grant available for the new programme.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When they transfer programmes, the subsidised semesters already used count against the tuition grant available for the new programme.

sections.label: One-time course-correction allowance
sections.summary: It asks whether there could be a limited, one-time course-correction allowance for a first transfer made during the first year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could there be a limited, one-time course-correction allowance for a first transfer made during the first year?

sections.label: Return after leaving for venture
sections.summary: A worker who leaves a job to pursue a venture should be able to return to employment, regardless of the venture's eventual outcome.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A worker who leaves a job to pursue a venture should be able to return to employment, regardless of the venture's eventual outcome.

sections.label: Bettr Group coffee and training
sections.summary: Bettr Group is a homegrown specialty coffee company that combines its business with training and inclusive employment for people facing social and economic barriers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Consider Bettr Group, it is a homegrown specialty coffee company that combines its business with training and inclusive employment for people facing social and economic barriers.

sections.label: Worker development and ESR
sections.summary: The ESR calls for AI to augment workers through job redesign and training, and for learning to be integrated with real work and employers' needs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They should also see a path to develop and progress.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This builds on the ESR, which calls for AI to augment workers through job redesign and training, and for learning to be integrated more closely with real work and employers' needs.

sections.label: Pay for greater responsibility
sections.summary: Where workers take on greater responsibilities and help generate productivity gains, this should be reflected in their pay or greater autonomy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Where workers take on greater responsibilities and help generate productivity gains, this should be reflected in their pay or greater autonomy over their work and time.

sections.label: Reciprocal commitment and amended Motion
sections.summary: Workers and innovation flourish together only through reciprocal commitment, and the speaker supports the Motion as amended by Mr Edward Chia.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Workers and innovation can flourish together, but only through a reciprocal commitment: workers must adapt and employers must create more valuable work and share the gains.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would have preferred a more nuanced and calibrated formulation, one that preserves its aspirations while making the trade-offs and responsibilities clearer.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That said, the amendments proposed by Mr Edward Chia brings the Motion closer to my position and it is more consistent with the points I have made.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And on balance, I would support the Motion as amended.

sections.label: Shortening retrenchment notification requirement
sections.summary: Thrust 6 calls to shorten the requirement for companies to submit a mandatory retrenchment notification within five working days after workers are notified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Thrust 6 makes a specific call to shorten the current requirement for companies to submit a mandatory retrenchment notification within five working days after workers are notified.

sections.label: Retrenchments April to June
sections.summary: It was reported that the 4,500 retrenchments from April to June this year were the highest since the last quarter of 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Within the story, it was reported that the 4,500 retrenchments from April to June this year were the highest since the last quarter of 2020.

sections.label: Rising recorded retrenchments
sections.summary: Recorded retrenchments increased from 6,440 in 2022 to 13,020 in 2024, and 14,490 in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this regard, two specific data points are noteworthy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, recorded retrenchments have increased in recent years from 6,440 in 2022 to 13,020 in 2024, and 14,490 in 2025.

sections.label: Retrenched workers lacking benefits
sections.summary: In 2024, potentially close to 3,000 retrenched workers in Singapore received no retrenchment benefits or less than the tripartite guidelines prescribe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Critically, though, what we can reasonably extrapolate from both these data points is that in 2024, for example, potentially close to 3,000 retrenched workers in Singapore either received no retrenchment benefits at all or received less than what is prescribed by the tripartite guidelines.

sections.label: Tribunal on retrenchment benefits
