sections.summary: In JIF v JIG, the Employment Claims Tribunal held that section 45 of the Employment Act does not create a statutory entitlement to retrenchment benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In JIF v JIG, the Employment Claims Tribunal held that section 45 of the Employment Act does not create a statutory entitlement to retrenchment benefits.

sections.label: DBS data on younger Singaporeans
sections.summary: DBS's 2025 financial wellness series found Gen Zs and Millennials aged 25 to 44 are falling behind older counterparts in retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to DBS Bank's 2025 instalment of its financial wellness series, which analysed aggregated and anonymised data from approximately two million DBS and POSB retail customers, Gen Zs and Millennials aged 25 to 44 are increasingly shouldering heavier liabilities and are falling behind their older counterparts in building retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Among pre-retirement age groups, those aged 35 to 44 are the most financially stretched, with debts slightly overweighing liquid assets, largely due to housing vehicle and credit card loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: CPF contributions stop, retirement balances grow more slowly, housing obligations continue, healthcare expenses continue, caregiving responsibilities continue.

sections.label: Employers' federation on Employment Act review
sections.summary: The Singapore National Employers' Federation cautioned that the Employment Act review should not inadvertently mandate practices reducing employer flexibilities and undermining competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, when the Government announced the review of the Employment Act last year, the Singapore National Employers' Federation cautioned that the review should not, and I quote, "inadvertently mandate progressive employment practices that may reduce flexibilities for employers and undermine business competitiveness".

sections.label: Facts on retrenchment benefit benchmarks
sections.summary: Collective agreements already prescribe retrenchment benefits, and most employers converge at those benchmarks, with few paying more than one month per year of service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, the facts do not fully support this concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are already collective agreements that prescribe retrenchment benefits and the vast majority of employers converge at those benchmarks anyway, with a very small number paying more than the one-month norm for each year of service.

sections.label: Employers already providing retrenchment benefits
sections.summary: Eight out of 10 eligible employees already receive retrenchment benefits up to the tripartite guideline of two weeks salary for every year of service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Those concerns deserve attention and respect, because it is neither simple nor straightforward to start, build or sustain a business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, we should not forget that many responsible employers already provide retrenchment benefits: eight out of 10 eligible employees already receive retrenchment benefits up to the tripartite guideline of two weeks salary for every year of service.

sections.label: Subsidiary legislation for higher payouts
sections.summary: Subsidiary legislation could direct higher retrenchment payouts for larger firms, up to one month's salary per year of service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A statutory framework could also be enhanced by subsidiary legislation directing higher payouts for larger firms, such as up to the union norm of one month salary for every year of service, something which larger global MNCs in particular would not necessarily baulk at, especially since they are already subject to legislative regimes governing retrenchment benefits in other countries where they operate.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefit backstop approaches
sections.summary: Some countries use national insurance schemes, wage guarantee agreements, or treat retrenchment benefits as preferential debt in insolvency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some create backstops, such as national insurance schemes, while others advance wage guarantee agreements, while yet others treat retrenchment benefits as a preferential debt through insolvency laws.

sections.label: Call for statutory retrenchment benefits framework
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to convene employers, unions and workers to develop a statutory retrenchment benefits framework and supports the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Trust and commitment to an employer is strengthened when workers know that after years of service, if restructuring occurs through no fault of their own, they will receive fair and meaningful protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Therefore, as part of the Government's implementation of the ESR, I urge the Government to convene employers, unions and workers to develop a statutory retrenchment benefits framework with the objective of introducing legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A resilient society requires workers who know they will not be left to bear the burdens of economic change alone, because in line with the call of the Labour Movement in NTUC, no less, while not every job can be protected, every worker deserves protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I support the original Motion in the names of Members Kenneth Tiong and Jamus Lim, which calls for an inclusive and equal economy for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We have been in session for close to five and a half hours, so I propose to take a break.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the chair at 4.20 pm.

sections.label: Singapore adult skills compared to OECD
sections.summary: Singapore tops test scores of 15-year-olds but ranks only mid-pack among OECD economies in adult literacy and numeracy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore tops the world in test scores of 15-year-olds, but can we top the world in the skills and learning agility of 45-year-olds?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development's (OECD's) survey of adult skills suggest that we are only in the middle of the pack relative to OECD economies in adult literacy and numeracy.

sections.label: Formal training not applied at work
sections.summary: Research suggests much formal training is not applied at work due to lack of opportunity or unconducive workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A body of research, including findings from the Institute for Adult Learning's Skills and Learning Survey, suggests that much of what people learn in formal training is not applied at work, often because there is no opportunity to do so, or because the workplace is not conducive.

sections.label: Skills-first practices and learning roles
sections.summary: Leaders, HR, managers and unions enable learning, and organisations should adopt skills-first practices for hiring and advancement.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Leaders, human resource (HR) professionals, line managers and unions all have a role to play in enabling learning by activating mindsets, securing training resources, embedding learning and work, and creating conducive environments for learning and experimentation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It should also be a priority for organisations to adopt skills-first practices, where skills, rather than credentials, become the key consideration for hiring, career development and advancement.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This will give employers access to a larger pool of talent, while workers will enjoy greater career mobility as they are not limited by their previous educational qualifications or work experience, but can leverage the skills they have picked up through work to take on new job roles or cross into other sectors.

sections.label: Institute of Adult Learning framework
sections.summary: The Institute of Adult Learning will launch a skills-first framework for action in October setting out actions and behaviours for individuals, employers and training providers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Institute of Adult Learning will be launching a skills-first framework for action in October, which will set out concrete actions and behaviours that we hope will become widely adopted by individuals, employers and training providers.

sections.label: Skills credentialing for sectors
sections.summary: The Institute of Adult Learning has pioneered skills credentialing for the training and adult education sector and is working with partner agencies to adapt it for other sectors.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Institute of Adult Learning has pioneered skills credentialing for the training and adult education sector, and we are working with partner agencies to adapt this methodology for other sectors.

sections.label: Personalised career guidance investment
sections.summary: There is scope to further invest in personalised career guidance and job-matching capabilities, recommending jobs based on skills, values, aspirations and personality fit.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Fourth, there is scope to further invest in personalised career guidance and job-matching capabilities, not just recommending jobs based on skills, but also on values, aspirations and personality fit.

sections.label: Support for micro entrepreneurship
sections.summary: The Government could review supporting ventures through financing, access to AI compute, business networks, mentoring or other targeted support to encourage micro entrepreneurship.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government could review what more could be done to support such ventures, whether through financing, access to AI compute, business networks and mentoring, or other targeted forms of support to encourage micro entrepreneurship as a viable career pathway or source of supplementary income for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Lifelong learning and employability expertise
sections.summary: Singapore needs to build up expertise in lifelong learning and employability, as it has in pedagogy for school-age children.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Just as we have built up considerable expertise in pedagogy that has placed Singapore at the forefront of global education for school-age children, we need to similarly build up expertise in lifelong learning and employability.

sections.label: ESR members and committees
sections.summary: Of the members and five committees involved in the ESR, it appears to mainly comprise C-suite and NTUC union leaders.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Of the members and five committees involved in the ESR, it appears to mainly comprise C-suite and the NTUC union leaders.

sections.label: ESR Thrust 5 AI-resilient sectors
sections.summary: Thrust 5 of the ESR recommended improving the attractiveness of AI-resilient sectors such as allied health, early childhood education and social work.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In this line, Thrust 5 of the ESR recommended that we improve the attractiveness of AI-resilient sectors, such as allied health, early childhood education and social work.

sections.label: Median wages of nurses, social workers, preschool teachers
sections.summary: Latest MOM data as of June 2025 shows median gross monthly wages of $5,129 for registered nurses, $4,565 for social workers and $4,150 for preschool teachers.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Latest MOM data as of June 2025 indicates the median gross wage earned by registered nurses at $5,129 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Social workers earn $4,565, preschool teachers earn $4,150.

sections.label: 2022 study on public healthcare burnout
sections.summary: A 2022 study in the Academy of Medicine, Singapore's journal found 37.8% of respondents had high emotional exhaustion, 29.7% high de-personalisation and 55.3% low personal accomplishment scores.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A 2022 study published in the Academy of Medicine, Singapore's official journal measuring burnout in the public healthcare sector between July 2019 and January 2020 found that 37.8% of respondents had high emotional exhaustion scores; 29.7% had high de-personalisation scores and 55.3% had low personal accomplishment scores.

sections.label: Care economy investment and informal caregiving
sections.summary: The VentureForGood Grant supports social enterprises up to $300,000, and a Duke-NUS study valued informal caregiving for seniors at $1.28 billion annually.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the current existence of the VentureForGood Grant administered by raiSE SG supports early and growth-stage social enterprises for up to $300,000 in capital expenditure and operating costs, how can we support more startups and commercial enterprises in this space to bring sustainable investments into the care economy? raiSE SG must work with the Ministry of Trade and Industry, and the Ministry of Social and Family Development jointly to review the care economy investment ecosystem to build a more sustainable investment and employment ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Caregiving is also borne by informal carers, such as family and friends.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This labour of love is not reflected in GDP figures, but its importance is underscored by the inaugural Duke-National University of Singapore study, which valued the economic contribution of informal caregiving for seniors at $1.28 billion annually.

sections.label: SME growth capital and listing path
sections.summary: The ESR report acknowledges SMEs find it difficult to secure growth stage capital, and suggests ESG work with SGX on governance and disclosure for co-invested companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For SME looking to scale, the ESR report acknowledges that companies still find it difficult to secure growth stage capital and that Temasek already participates in SME co-investment.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore-co-invested companies, through the Startup SG Equity Scheme, should be re) mainboard or catalyst, and ESG should work with SGX on governance and disclosure requirements for co-invested companies to ease the path to listing.

sections.label: Business failure and personal bankruptcy
sections.summary: A Straits Times article on 26 May indicated business failure is among the top reasons individuals go into personal bankruptcy.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: After I spoke in early May this year about supporting entrepreneurship amongst youths, including a call to adapt our current bankruptcy framework, a Straits Times' article on 26 May indicated that business failure is among the top reasons why individuals go into personal bankruptcy.

sections.label: EU second chance policy
sections.summary: An EU expert group report said second chance policy for bankrupt entrepreneurs may aid company creation and job growth, and the EU adopted a preventive restructuring approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A European Union (EU) expert group report in 2011 that, "A second chance policy that enables formally bankrupt entrepreneurs to restart may represent one of the most promising and under-exploited policy options for company creation and job growth." The EU has since adopted a more balanced preventive restructuring approach for bona fide entrepreneurs seeking a second chance.

sections.label: Data centres moved to Johor
sections.summary: The 2019 moratorium on new data centres and higher operating costs drove operators to Johor and Batam, with Singaporean companies owning the largest capacity share there.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The earlier 2019 moratorium on new data centres, as well as higher operating costs here, drove operators to set up shop in neighbouring Johor and Batam, with Singaporean companies owning the largest proportion of data centre capacity in both regions.

sections.label: Forest clearing and resource use
sections.summary: Concern is mounting over forests cut for housing and development, while EMA noted electricity consumption rose 4% in 2024 and PUB expects non-domestic water use to rise.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Concern is mounting over forests being cut down for housing, both at Maju Forest and Gillman Barracks, alongside a patch of forest near Woodlands Checkpoint, which would be cleared for the development of a new commercial hub, while over 52 hectares of forested land would be cut down for the next phase of the Jurong Innovation District.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: EMA noted that electricity consumption increased by 4% year-on-year in 2024, with commerce and service-related businesses consuming the highest proportion that year at 40.2% of our total electricity use.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Already, non-domestic water consumption takes up 55% of our total water use and PUB estimates that this is expected to increase to 60% by 2065.

sections.label: Future economy felt by workers
sections.summary: Many Singaporean workers and business owners already feel the future economy through uncertain demand, rising costs, sharper competition and fast-changing technologies and industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: For many Singaporean workers and business owners, the future economy is already being felt in very real ways in uncertain demand, rising costs, sharper competition, new technologies and industries that are changing faster than ever before.

sections.label: AI disrupting jobs
sections.summary: AI will disrupt jobs at a speed and scale not seen before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: AI will disrupt jobs at a speed and scale that we have not seen before.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefits and unemployment support
sections.summary: On retrenchment benefits and unemployment support, NTUC and the Labour Movement have worked with tripartite partners to ensure no worker is left behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: There are two topics in this space, firstly, on retrenchment benefits and unemployment support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: And on the topic of mandating retrenchment benefits, the NTUC and the Labour Movement, including myself, have been working with tripartite partners to ensure that no worker is left behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In fact, we have been trying to lobby, myself inclusive, in this House, for the past decade, including earlier this year, for further strengthening of the retrenchment protection regime here in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: On the topic of unemployment insurance support, this is something I spoke about more than a decade ago, lobbying for some form of unemployment support for workers in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am very happy that it has been introduced last year, on 26 April – I remember the fateful date – the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme was implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)

sections.label: Ecosystems and innovation system
sections.summary: The speaker says startups need to tap ecosystems like the Institution of Engineers and that the Motion must include the system of innovation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
sentences.text: As far as the Motion is concerned, it is not just assisting, it is not just getting startup, giving resources to push them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
sentences.text: I think the Motion has to include the system of innovation.

sections.label: NUS Overseas Colleges startups

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In fact, just end-June, I met eight startups at NUS Homecoming, from the very same programme that Minister of State Dinesh mentioned, NUS Overseas Colleges.

sections.label: Thriving Singaporeans and businesses
sections.summary: The speaker's central argument is that thriving Singaporeans drive thriving Singapore businesses, and thriving businesses build a thriving Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: My central argument today is simple: thriving Singaporeans drive thriving Singapore businesses, and thriving Singapore businesses build a thriving Singapore.

sections.label: 5Cs for business growth
sections.summary: The speaker says good ideas need customers, capital, connections, capabilities and confidence to grow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: When businesses do well, workers should share in the gains.

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]
sentences.text: I have seen our enterprise landscapes from several perspectives, having worked in a successful startup, supporting Singapore companies in the Public Service and now running an SME.

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]
sentences.text: These experiences have convinced me that good ideas need "5Cs" to grow: customers, capital, connections, capabilities and confidence.

sections.label: Customer and track record barrier

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]

sections.label: Lead demand for sectors
sections.summary: Companies in four sectors face similar barriers, so the speaker welcomes mobilising lead demand from large companies and the public sector.

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]
sentences.text: Singapore companies in sustainability, advanced manufacturing, healthcare and enterprise technology encounter similar barriers.

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]
sentences.text: I therefore welcome the ESR's recommendation to mobilise lead demand from large companies and the public sector.

sections.label: Procurement for new entrants
sections.summary: Buyers could weight verified performance, certifications, pilot results and delivery capacity, and use smaller or phased contracts where risks are manageable.

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]
sentences.text: For suitable purchases involving new solutions, agencies and major buyers could give greater weight to independently verified technical performance, relevant certifications, pilot results and delivery capacity.

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]
sentences.text: And where the risks are manageable, smaller initial contracts or phased procurement can allow credible new entrants to establish a track record without requiring the buyer to assume the full risk from the outset.

sections.label: Measuring effectiveness by outcomes
sections.summary: Effectiveness should be measured by partnerships formed, standards attained, projects commercialised and contracts secured, not membership or events.

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]
sentences.text: Its effectiveness should therefore be measured not by membership or the number of events organised, but by partnerships formed, standards attained, projects commercialised and contracts secured.

sections.label: Penguin green loan ferries

sentences.text: After securing Shell as a customer, Penguin obtained a green loan under the Enterprise Financing Scheme – Green to support the design, construction and operation of Singapore's first fully electric seagoing passenger ferries and their rapid shore chargers.

sections.label: Tracking company progression stages

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]
sentences.text: These figures tell us whether support has been delivered, but not whether enterprises have progressed.

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]
sentences.text: We should also track how many companies move from pilot to first contract, from first contract to export and from export to scale.

sections.label: Evaluating enterprise policy by progression
sections.summary: Enterprise policy should be evaluated by progression, not merely by participation.

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]
sentences.text: Enterprise policy should therefore be evaluated not merely by participation, but by progression.

sections.label: Investing in SME leader capabilities
sections.summary: Investment in SME owners, directors and business leaders should help them interpret technologies, assess overseas opportunities, understand financing, manage people and decide when to adapt, expand, pivot or diversify.

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]
sentences.text: We must also invest in the capabilities of SME owners, directors and business leaders.

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]
sentences.text: It should help them interpret new technologies, assess overseas opportunities, understand financing options, manage people and decide when to adapt, expand, pivot or diversify.

sections.label: Supporting responsible entrepreneurs
sections.summary: Responsible entrepreneurs need mentorship, suitable financing, strong networks and a reasonable second chance after honest commercial failure, and genuine commercial failure must be distinguished from misconduct.

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]
sentences.text: An owner may invest personal savings, guarantee a loan and forgo a salary during difficult months, while remaining responsible for paying employees, suppliers and creditors on time.

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]
sentences.text: Responsible entrepreneurs need mentorship, suitable financing, strong networks and a reasonable second chance after honest commercial failure.

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]
sentences.text: An economy that wants entrepreneurs to experiment must distinguish genuine commercial failure from misconduct.

sections.label: Wage growth and productivity
sections.summary: Sustained real wage growth must be supported by higher productivity, stronger capabilities and businesses creating greater value, with workers sharing gains through better wages, career progression and skilled roles.

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]
sentences.text: Wage standards provide an important floor, but sustained real wage growth must also be supported by higher productivity, stronger capabilities and businesses that create greater value.

sentences.speaker: [Mr Speaker in the Chair]
sentences.text: Crucially, workers must share in these gains through better wages, stronger career progression and greater opportunities to take on skilled and leadership roles.

sections.label: Progression, people and ESR recommendations
sections.summary: Enterprise policy should be evaluated by progression from pilot to first contract, export and scale, and the ESR recommendations set out how to get there for businesses and workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
sentences.text: — we should evaluate enterprise policy by progression, not merely participation; whether companies move from pilot to first contract; from first contract to export; and from export to scale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
sentences.text: Ultimately, an economy for the future must be built around its people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
sentences.text: Our task is now to give Singaporeans a fair chance to build, grow and lead successful businesses from Singapore, and the ESR recommendations set out how we can get there for both businesses and workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
sentences.text: I support the Motion as amended, especially Part (b), where local and global enterprises should be interacting with each other and not grow in isolation.

sections.label: ESR Committees engagement numbers
sections.summary: Five ESR Committees engaged more than 7,700 people over nine months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Five ESR Committees engaged more than 7,700 people over nine months.

sections.label: Support for MNCs and SMEs
sections.summary: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim suggested the Government supports SMEs less than MNCs and that Singapore must pivot to SMEs, but the response says both must succeed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim suggested that the Government is not supporting our own SMEs as much as we do for MNCs and that we must pivot away from MNCs to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: For our economy to thrive, we need both MNCs and SMEs in Singapore to succeed.

sections.label: Grants and loans for SMEs
sections.summary: The Government provides nearly $2 billion yearly in direct grants and loans for local SMEs, and the Ministry of Finance stands ready with more resources if demand grows.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Every year, the Government provides nearly $2 billion dollars in direct grants and loans for our local SMEs to build stronger capabilities, embark on new projects and compete successfully in global markets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: We can do more to help our companies make fuller use of the support available.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: And if demand for these schemes grows because more companies are stepping up and making use of them, let me state for the record that the Ministry of Finance stands ready in support with more resources.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore supporting local companies
sections.summary: In 2018 MTI agencies were reorganised to form Enterprise Singapore, a Statutory Board supporting local companies end-to-end in capability building, innovation, financing, talent and internationalisation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Building a business requires many factors: stronger leadership, deep technological capabilities, access to capital and talent, and the confidence to venture overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: That is why in 2018, we re-organised agencies in MTI to form Enterprise Singapore – a new Statutory Board with a clear mission to support our local companies end-to-end: capability building, innovation, financing, talent, internationalisation.

sections.label: Singapore Economic Resilience Task Force
sections.summary: The Singapore Economic Resilience Task Force, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong, was set up after US Liberation Day tariffs to help businesses adapt, with Castlery diversifying its manufacturing base with Enterprise Singapore's support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: It is the reverse: to strengthen our companies to compete more effectively in more overseas markets with greater resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: This is why following the US Liberation Day tariffs last year, we set up the Singapore Economic Resilience Task Force, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong, to help our businesses adapt.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: For example, Castlery, an online furniture company with 70% of its revenue from the US, has diversified its manufacturing base with Enterprise Singapore's support.

sections.label: Singaporeans in MNC senior management
sections.summary: More than two-thirds of senior management positions in MNCs in Singapore today are held by Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: More than two-thirds of senior management positions in MNCs in Singapore today are held by Singaporeans.

sections.label: Applied Materials Tampines campus investment
sections.summary: Mr Saktiandi said Applied Materials recently invested in a second campus at Tampines, which they described with excitement when the speaker visited their first Upper Changi facility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Mr Saktiandi mentioned that Applied Materials had invested recently in building a second campus at Tampines; they told me about it with great excitement when I visited their first facility at Upper Changi.

sections.label: Investment resources and local enterprises
sections.summary: Resources for attracting investments do not come at the expense of local enterprises, and reducing ecosystem support risks MNCs leaving and local companies operating elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: The resources we commit to attracting investments do not come at the expense of supporting local enterprises.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: If we reduce the resources that we commit to supporting this ecosystem, then only do we risk MNCs leaving Singapore, even local companies will think about operating in other jurisdictions.

sections.label: ESR outcomes and whole-of-society effort
sections.summary: The speaker supports Mr Edward Chia's amended Motion, saying the ESR will be judged by outcomes like better jobs and incomes, and requires a whole-of-society effort.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: We are not choosing between domestic demand and external markets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: This is why I fully support the amendments to the Motion as proposed by Mr Edward Chia, which reflect our economic strategy holistically and accurately.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Ultimately, the ESR is not going to be judged by the number of schemes we create, or the amount of money we spend.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: It will be judged by its outcomes: better jobs, higher incomes, more social mobility and greater resilience, and whether Singaporeans have the confidence that they can build better lives for themselves and for their children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: This is why it is important that the ESR is a whole-of-society effort, led by a new generation of business, union, society and Government leaders, who will collectively own these outcomes.

sections.label: Tripartite Guidelines worker compensation review
sections.summary: The Government is looking at whether compensation can go above 90%, is not wedded to legislating it, and will consult SNEF and unions before deciding.

sentences.text: As the Member knows, with the Tripartite Guidelines, at least nine and 10 workers are compensated, as was highlighted.

sentences.text: We are looking at it, because we have highlighted that both in the speech and as well as the ESR has recommended for stronger support to our workers.

sentences.text: Whether or not we can go above 90% is something that we are looking at as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: We are not at this point wedded on whether or not it is to be legislated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: As in all things that the Government does, we will consult Singapore National Employers Federation, we will consult the unions and make a considered decision after our consults.

sections.label: Singaporeans sharing economic success
sections.summary: A Singaporean gets a lasting share of success through good jobs, real wage growth, relevant skills, and support to recover and build again after setbacks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: A Singaporean gets a lasting share of that success by meaningfully participating in our economy, through good jobs, sustained real wages growth and finding fulfilment through work; by acquiring and building skills and skillsets that remain relevant as technology evolves and changes; and after any setbacks, by taking up the opportunity to learn, and the support to recover and build again.

sections.label: Three ESR imperatives
sections.summary: The ESR is guided by three imperatives: sharpen Singapore's value proposition, enhance agility and adaptability of firms, workers and institutions, and build resilience alongside efficiency.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The ESR is guided by three imperatives: sharpen Singapore's value proposition; enhance the agility and adaptability of our firms, workers and institutions; and build resilience alongside efficiency.

sections.label: Fairness versus equality in policy
sections.summary: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh distinguished fairness from equality alone as a guide for policy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh made a useful distinction: fairness, rather than equality alone, should guide policy.

sections.label: Global and local enterprises

sections.label: Industry R&D employment and spinoffs

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)

sentences.text: Through the Technology for Enterprise Capability Upgrading (T-UP) programme, A*STAR research scientists and engineers can be seconded to support local SMEs' R&D projects for up to two years.

sections.label: RIE2030 research funding commitment

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)

sections.label: Startup and equities market financing

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Eighty companies in its first seven cohorts generated a combined $2.5 billion in additional revenue within three years; and $1 billion came from overseas expansion.

sections.label: Global Innovation Alliance support

sections.label: ESR career bridges proposal

sentences.text: The ESR proposes “career bridges” linking workers in at-risk roles to more resilient occupations through training, guidance and job matching.

sections.label: Helping workers navigate change

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Our objective must be to help each person return confidently to sustainable work – not merely to make unemployment more bearable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will not be able to promise that every job will remain unchanged – I do not think we can or should we even try to do that – hold back technology merely to freeze roles in place.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)

sentences.text: The amended Motion, Mr Speaker, captures the full combination that Singapore needs: an equal and inclusive economy with opportunities for entrepreneurs, households, businesses and workers, and ideas and innovation to flourish; and an economy powered by dynamic local companies and global enterprises, healthy domestic and external demand, and Singaporeans and Singaporean capital venturing abroad.

sections.label: Government's role in economy
sections.summary: The Government will maintain a trusted, open economy, invest long term, address gaps and help workers prepare for change.

sentences.text: The Government will play its part: maintaining a trusted, open economy; investing for the long term; addressing genuine capability, financing and market-access gaps; and helping workers prepare for change.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)

sections.summary: Competition is now global against countries like China and the US, and can be eased with support from Enterprise Singapore, SBF and MTI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman
sentences.text: My point of clarification is this: we compete in a global scale now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman
sentences.text: What we compete before, purely on company to company; and now we compete against China, against US, against everybody.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman
sentences.text: And my point is that in the context of Singapore's unique strategy, the competition can be made easier with the help of what our company has grown.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman
sentences.text: We have the support of Enterprise Singapore, SBF, we have the support of MTI and so forth.

sections.label: MTI renaming and Cabinet reshuffle
sections.summary: MTI will be renamed Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry from 1 October 2026, with DPM Gan overseeing trade and the speaker energy and industry.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In fact, if you look at the renaming and the most recent Cabinet reshuffling, the Ministry of Trade and Industry will be renamed as Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry with effect from 1 October 2026.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Our Prime Minister is enlightened, he has seen how potentially all of the disruptions, the expanse of the opportunities that are available.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And therefore, given the size and the scope of what we all have to do, Deputy Prime Minister Gan in his experience, overseeing trade and the macroeconomic strategy; and I will look at energy and industry, and I will actively engage the trade associations and chambers.

sections.label: Motion answers economic worries
sections.summary: The Motion was filed to answer Singaporeans' economic worries about jobs, work, flats, rent, courses, wages and building something.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Speaker, I thank every Member who spoke on both sides of this House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We filed this Motion to provide answers to the economic worries top-of-mind for every Singaporean: whether there is a job and whether it lasts; whether the young person who has done everything asked of them can find work that goes somewhere; whether a flat is within reach; whether a small shop can survive its rent; whether the course a worker is sent on leads to a job; whether the growth we announced is felt in a wage; whether a Singaporean who wants to build something can afford to do it in spite of the high cost structure here.

sections.label: Special zone near NTU
sections.summary: He proposed a special zone around NTU where state land is charged at development cost rather than market scarcity value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, how do we foster a dynamic innovation ecosystem that can overcome and maximise value in spite of high business cost and physical constraints?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I proposed a special zone around NTU, where state land is charged at development cost rather than market scarcity value.

sections.label: Tenders, compute, Fair Start Promise
sections.summary: He proposed concept and price tenders for strategic sites and an HDB model for compute, while Mr Andre Low proposed a Fair Start Promise for young Singaporeans under 30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He proposed concept and price tenders as the default for strategic sites, because a system where the highest bidder wins, the reserve price is unpublished and unawarded sites simply can wait, can only ratchet upward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And he proposed an "HDB model for compute", because we take some $20 billion a year in land sales and set aside only about $150 million for a one-year compute programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Andre Low proposed a Fair Start Promise, a national commitment to work towards a simple goal that young Singaporeans under 30, making the transition from education or NS into working life will get a fair start through stable employment or a proper paid career-building pathway.

sections.label: Dinesh agrees with Fair Start
sections.summary: Minister of State Dinesh broadly agreed with Mr Andre Low's proposals and shared the aspiration of giving every young Singaporean a fair start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Minister of State Dinesh broadly agreed with Mr Andre Low's proposals and acknowledged that he shared our aspiration of giving every young Singaporean a fair start.

sections.label: Universal redundancy insurance scheme
sections.summary: Mr Fadli Fawzi proposed a universal redundancy insurance scheme funded by employer and employee contributions, paying 40% of last drawn pay capped at 40% of median for up to six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Fadli Fawzi proposed a universal redundancy insurance scheme, employer and employee together combining one-tenth of 1% of monthly salary, paying 40% of last drawn pay, capped at 40% of median, up to six months, with no application to make, because a worker who must apply and may be refused cannot plan.

sections.label: Statutory retrenchment benefits floor
sections.summary: He proposed legislating a statutory floor for retrenchment benefits at two weeks' salary per year of service, with higher payouts for larger firms, because the Courts confirmed a gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As a matter of law, currently, there is nothing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He proposed legislating a statutory floor for retrenchment benefits at a tripartite norm of two weeks' salary for each year of service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He also proposed subsidiary legislation directing higher payouts for larger firms, up to the union norm of a month's salary a year and he proposed doing it now because the Courts have confirmed a gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This year, the Employment Claims Tribunals held that section 45 of the Employment Act creates no entitlement, and the tripartite guidelines create no legal basis, for one.

sections.label: Caregiver compensation and time use studies
sections.summary: She proposed compensation for family caregivers, expanded respite care and regular official time use studies, noting informal caregiving for seniors was valued at $1.28 billion a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A wage floor was not built currently to reach them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: She proposed compensation for family caregivers, expanded respite care and regular official time use studies, because informal caregiving for seniors was valued at $1.28 billion a year and appears in no national account.

sections.label: WP rejects Amendment No 1
sections.summary: The WP cannot accept Amendment No 1, which deletes "notwithstanding" and inserts "in line with".

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On Amendment No 1, to delete "notwithstanding" and insert "in line with", the WP cannot accept this amendment.

sections.label: WP stance on amendments
sections.summary: The WP accepts Amendment Nos 2 and 4, had reservations on No 3, and says the ESR proceeds regardless.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The ESR proceeds, our belief stands on the record, and neither one decides the other.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We have no issues accepting Amendment Nos 2 and No 4.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We had some reservations accepting Amendment No 3.

sections.label: WP accepts Amendment No 3
sections.summary: The WP calls the suggestion a false binary and strawman, but will accept Amendment No 3 without nitpicking semantics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Suggesting otherwise is a false binary and it is a convenient strawman, but it is not an argument that we are making.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, we will not nitpick on the semantics of Amendment No 3 and hence, will accept this amendment.

sections.label: Recurring committee ambitions
sections.summary: Four committees from 2010 to 2026 repeated near identical ambitions: move up the value chain, grow champions, internationalise, reskill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The 2010 Economic Strategies Committee, the 2017 Committee on the Future Economy, the 2021 Emerging Stronger Taskforce, and now this 2026 Review, with the same ambitions recurring in near identical language across all four: move up the value chain; grow homegrown champions; internationalise; reskill.

sections.label: 2010 committee targets
sections.summary: The 2010 committee set productivity and enterprise targets; the productivity goal was met, the 1,000-company goal was not tracked after 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The 2010 Economic Strategies Committee set two targets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One on productivity – to "achieve productivity growth of 2% to 3% per year over the next 10 years." This goal was met.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One on enterprises – "We can raise this number significantly to reach 1,000 such enterprises over the next 10 years." Local companies with revenue over $100 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This goal of 1,000 local companies with revenue over $100 million was not tracked after 2017, when the report recorded about 800 such companies.

sections.label: Manufacturing share of GDP
sections.summary: Manufacturing was 17.4% of GDP in 2016 and remains 17.4% in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Manufacturing was 17.4% of GDP in 2016 and remains 17.4% in 2025.

sections.label: No consensus on amended Motion
sections.summary: Three of four amendments are accounted for, but consensus on the amended Motion failed over the term "notwithstanding".

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: So, that accounts for three of the four amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: We regret that we are not able to achieve consensus on the amended Motion today, that the disagreement has founded on the term "notwithstanding", as opposed to what we are proposing, which is in line with the ESR.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefits and cash flow
sections.summary: The Member asks whether mandatory payments of at least one month for larger companies could push firms with cash flow issues into deeper distress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: The current norm actually ranges between two weeks and one month salary per year of service, but the Member has proposed at least one month for larger companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: And for those they are facing serious cash flow issues, if such payments are mandatory, would the Member not agree that this push might weaken firms into deeper distress and potentially putting remaining jobs at risk?

sections.label: Statutory minimum as standard
sections.summary: The Member asks whether a statutory minimum could become the standard, with higher-paying firms paying only the prescribed amount.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: Could the statutory minimum instead become the standard, with firms that are currently paying more choosing to pay only the prescribed amount, leaving less room for negotiation, even in unionised companies?

sections.label: Security for retrenched workers
sections.summary: The Member states the best security for a retrenched worker is not only a payout but the ability to find the next good job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: Because ultimately, the best security for a retrenched worker is not only a payout, but the ability to find the next good job.

sections.label: Amendment No 1 wording
sections.summary: Amendment No 1 deletes "not withstanding" in line 1 and inserts "in line with", and the Question is put.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Amendment No 1 is, "In line 1, to delete 'not withstanding' and insert 'in line with'." The Question is, “That Amendment No 1 be made”.

sections.label: Amendments Nos 2 to 4
sections.summary: Amendments Nos 2, 3 and 4 are stated and the Question is put on the amended Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker:
sentences.text: Amendment No 2 is, "In line 5, to delete 'economic engine driven' and insert 'economy powered'."

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Amendment No 3, "In line 5, after the words 'local companies', to insert 'global enterprises,'."

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Amendment No 4, "In line 5, after the words 'healthy domestic', to insert 'and external'."

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The question is, "That this House, in line with the suggestions in the Economic Strategy Review on the future Singapore economy, believes: (a) in a more equal and inclusive economy, with opportunities for entrepreneurs to experiment, households and businesses to succeed, workers to thrive, and ideas and innovation to flourish; and (b) in an economy powered by dynamic local companies, global enterprises, healthy domestic and external demand, and Singaporeans and Singaporean capital venturing abroad." Those who agree say "Aye".
